stemMarkdown: If 10 men working 8 hours a day complete a job in 6 days, how many days will 6 men working 10 hours a day take to complete the same job? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: The job is $10 \times 6 \times 8 = 480$ man-hours. The new team supplies $6 \times 10 = 60$ man-hours per day, so it takes $\dfrac{480}{60} = 8.0$ days.
altSolutionMarkdown: Chain rule in one line: $\dfrac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \dfrac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$. Everything that supplies effort multiplies on top; the work done divides underneath.
